config.title: Accessibility (a11y) Fundamentals

intro.title: Accessibility (a11y) Fundamentals
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple, accessible form component that collects user information. You will learn the core concepts of web accessibility (a11y), focusing on semantic HTML, proper labeling, and keyboard navigation. The main technologies involved are Vue's template syntax, native HTML form elements, and ARIA attributes. By the end, you'll understand how to make your Vue applications usable for everyone, including people with disabilities.
intro.usecase: Accessibility fundamentals are essential in any public-facing web application to ensure all users, including those with disabilities, can interact with your product. For example, in a SaaS dashboard, proper ARIA labels on charts, keyboard navigation through data tables, and semantic HTML for filter panels allow screen reader users to understand and control the interface. As a developer, implementing these a11y patterns in Vue components—like accessible form validation messages or focus-trapped modals—is a standard requirement for compliance and inclusive user experience in real projects such as e-commerce sites, banking apps, or content management systems.

objectives: Implement semantic HTML elements within Vue components to improve screen reader navigation
Configure ARIA attributes on interactive Vue elements to communicate state and purpose
Construct keyboard-navigable interfaces by binding Vue event handlers to appropriate keys
Apply proper focus management techniques using Vue refs and lifecycle hooks
Integrate accessible form validation with Vue's reactive data and computed properties
Manipulate dynamic content announcements using Vue's reactivity system and ARIA live regions
Initialize accessible component patterns by combining Vue slots with semantic markup

steps.title: Import Vue and ref from vue
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the ref function from the vue package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and ref from 'vue'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing from a package
import { ref } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have Vue and ref available to use in your component.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Vue and ref.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Vue and ref from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.

steps.title: Create the main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named AccessibilityDemo with a default export and a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.hint: Use the Vue component structure with export default and setup function.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue and ref from 'vue'

// Create your AccessibilityDemo component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue component named AccessibilityDemo is created with proper setup structure.
successCriteria: Component is named AccessibilityDemo, has default export, and setup function returns empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main Vue component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have the component name, default export, and setup function returning an object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't quite right. Check the example and try again.

steps.title: Initialize reactive state for accessibility status
steps.instruction: Inside your AccessibilityDemo component, create a reactive state variable called isAccessible using Vue's ref and initialize it to true.
steps.hint: Use the ref function imported earlier to create a reactive reference with an initial value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating reactive state in Vue
const count = ref(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a reactive isAccessible state variable initialized to true.
successCriteria: The isAccessible variable is declared using ref() and initialized to true inside the setup() function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using ref() and initializing isAccessible to true.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using Vue's ref function to create a reactive variable called isAccessible with an initial value of true.

steps.title: Define a handler to toggle accessibility status
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named toggleAccessibility that toggles the value of isAccessible between true and false.
steps.hint: You can create a function that sets isAccessible.value to its opposite value using the logical NOT operator (!).
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a toggleAccessibility function that flips the boolean value of isAccessible when called.
successCriteria: The toggleAccessibility function is defined and correctly toggles the isAccessible ref value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it correctly toggles the isAccessible value. Check that you're using the logical NOT operator (!) on isAccessible.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleAccessibility function is missing or doesn't toggle the isAccessible value. Remember to create a function that sets isAccessible.value to !isAccessible.value.

steps.title: Return the reactive state and handler from setup
steps.instruction: In the setup function's return statement, add toggleAccessibility to the object so it can be used in the template.
steps.hint: The return statement should expose both isAccessible and toggleAccessibility. Add toggleAccessibility as a property in the returned object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The setup function returns both isAccessible and toggleAccessibility, making them available in the template.
successCriteria: The return statement includes both isAccessible and toggleAccessibility properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure toggleAccessibility is included in the return object along with isAccessible.
steps.feedbackWrong: The return statement should include both isAccessible and toggleAccessibility. Check the object syntax.

steps.title: Add a main container with semantic HTML
steps.instruction: In your component's template, add a main element that contains an h1 heading with the text 'Accessibility Demo'.
steps.hint: Use the main element as the primary container and include an h1 inside it. This provides semantic structure for screen readers.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: semantic container with heading

Page Title
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has semantic HTML structure with a main container and heading.
successCriteria: The template contains a main element with an h1 heading inside it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have both the main element and an h1 heading inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template should contain a main element with an h1 heading inside it.

steps.title: Display the current accessibility status
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add a paragraph element that displays the current accessibility status using text interpolation. Show the value of isAccessible.
steps.hint:
Use a

tag with double curly braces {{ }} to display the reactive state value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying reactive state in template

Current status: {{ isActive }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a paragraph displaying the current boolean value of isAccessible (true or false).
successCriteria: A paragraph element exists in the template that displays the isAccessible value using Vue's text interpolation syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the correct variable name 'isAccessible' inside double curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The paragraph displaying the accessibility status is missing or incorrect. Check that you've added a

tag with {{ isAccessible }}.

steps.title: Add a toggle button with proper ARIA attributes
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the main container that toggles the accessibility status. The button should have an @click binding to the toggleAccessibility handler, an aria-label describing its purpose, and an aria-pressed attribute bound to the isAccessible state.
steps.hint: Use the button element with @click="toggleAccessibility", aria-label="Toggle accessibility mode", and :aria-pressed="isAccessible".
steps.analogousExample:
// Accessible button example
<button 
  @click="handleClick"
  aria-label="Toggle feature"
  :aria-pressed="isActive"
>
  Toggle
</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The button will appear in the UI with proper ARIA attributes that update based on the accessibility status.
successCriteria: A button element is added with @click="toggleAccessibility", aria-label="Toggle accessibility mode", and :aria-pressed="isAccessible" attributes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but check if it has all required ARIA attributes: @click binding, aria-label, and aria-pressed bound to isAccessible.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or doesn't have the required ARIA attributes. Review the instruction to add @click="toggleAccessibility", aria-label="Toggle accessibility mode", and :aria-pressed="isAccessible".

steps.title: Add accessible form controls with labels
steps.instruction: Inside the template, after the toggle button, add a labeled text input field and a labeled select dropdown to demonstrate accessible form controls.
steps.hint: Use the <label> element with for attribute matching the input's id. For the select, include a default option.
steps.analogousExample:
// Accessible form controls example
<label for="name">Name:</label>
<input id="name" type="text" />

<label for="color">Favorite Color:</label>
<select id="color">
  <option value="">Select a color</option>
  <option value="red">Red</option>
</select>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have two accessible form controls: a text input with proper labeling and a select dropdown with proper labeling.
successCriteria: The template contains a labeled text input field and a labeled select dropdown with associated label elements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both a text input and a select dropdown, each with their own label element using the for attribute.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form controls are missing or not properly labeled. Remember to use <label> elements with for attributes matching the input/select ids.

steps.title: Add image with alt text and focus indicators
steps.instruction: Add an image element with descriptive alt text and a focusable element with tabindex inside the main container.
steps.hint:

steps.expectedOutcome: The component will include an accessible image with alt text and a focusable element to demonstrate keyboard navigation.
successCriteria: An element with alt attribute and a focusable element with tabindex='0' are added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some elements, but make sure to include both an image with alt text and a focusable element with tabindex.
steps.feedbackWrong: The required elements weren't added. Check the instruction for adding both an image with alt attribute and a focusable element.
